title: Connecting external AI agents to Zendesk (EAP)
snippet:
This article describes how to connect external AI agents to your Zendesk account. Connecting is a two-step process:
1. In Zendesk, configure a connection to an external AI agent that defines what you'll allow the external agent to do in your Zendesk account.
2. In your external agent's AI platform, connect your external AI agent to Zendesk with an MCP server URL specified in the connection you configured.

After configuring a connection to an external AI agent in your account, you can connect your external AI agent to Zendesk. There are two types of connections depending on what you want to use:
- To use tools, connect to the Zendesk MCP server
- To delegate tasks to a Zendesk AI agent, connect to the Zendesk agent using the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol
**To connect an external AI agent to Zendesk**
1. In [Admin Center](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4581766374554#topic_hfg_dyz_1hb), click ![](https://zen-marketing-documentation.s3.amazonaws.com/docs/en/icon_ai.png) **AI** in the sidebar, then select **External AI**.
2. Select the connection for the agent and click the **Setup** tab.
3. If you want your agent to use tools, copy the MCP server URL under **Tools**.
Example: `https://example.zendesk.com/mcp`
If available, click the link to open the detailed setup instructions and copy the command line interface (CLI) command to add the MCP server URL to your external agent. For example, the Claude CLI command looks as follows:
`claude mcp add --scope user --client-id '<OAuth client ID from Setup>' --transport http zendesk '<MCP server URL from Setup>'`
A CLI command provides you with an alternative way of adding the MCP server URL to your external agent.
4.

In Admin Center, go to AI > External AI, add a connection, choose a pre-built provider or bring your own provider, and define its access, tools, and any Zendesk AI agents it can use. Save the connection, then connect the agent in its AI platform using the MCP server URL or agent card URL from the connection’s Setup tab.

**How do I choose between the MCP server and the A2A agent connection?**
Use the Zendesk MCP server when you want the external agent to use Zendesk tools. Use the Zendesk AI agent connection with the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol when you want it to delegate tasks to a Zendesk AI agent. title: MCP Client Connector integration with Zendesk

# MCP Client
## Zendesk’s MCP Client allows you to easily connect your Zendesk instance to external MCP Servers.
### About this connector
OAuth-based connections
Our MCP Client takes care of Dynamic Client Registration, kicking off the OAuth flow, securely storing auth credentials, and securely using OAuth tokens to authenticate tool calls. For MCP Servers that require it, we also provide the ability to manually enter OAuth client details.
Tool discovery
Once connected the server’s MCP tools are discovered and processed to capture the tool names, descriptions, input fields, and (if provided by the server) output fields.
Tool management
Your Admins can select which tools they want to make available to Zendesk AI Agents and Action Flows.
Use tools in Action Flows
Tools are made available as steps to use in Action Flows, easily adding new third-party functionality to event-driven workflows, and AI use cases like Auto Assist, AI Agents, and Custom Agents.

title: Using the Zendesk MCP client to access MCP tools in action flows and advanced action flows
snippet:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets admins connect Zendesk to external MCP servers, discover the tools those servers provide, and use those tools as steps inaction flowsandadvanced action flows. This extends your Zendesk workflows to interact with third-party systems—such as project management tools, e-commerce platforms, or internal knowledge systems—without building custom API integrations.
Summary: ◀▼
Connect external MCP servers with OAuth, choose the tools you want to make available, and use them in action flows or advanced action flows to retrieve information or perform actions in third-party systems without building custom API integrations. Configure tool outputs to reuse data in later steps, and review and test flows when tools change.

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets admins connect Zendesk to external MCP servers, discover the tools those servers provide, and use those tools as steps in [action flows](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8855513857306) and [advanced action flows](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/11149728300186). This extends your Zendesk workflows to interact with third-party systems—such as project management tools, e-commerce platforms, or internal knowledge systems—without building custom API integrations.
MCP connections are created and managed in Admin Center. After you create a connection, Zendesk retrieves the available MCP tools from that server and displays them in the action builder so you can use them in workflows and, optionally, surface those flows through [auto assist](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8984493142810), [AI agents](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/6970583409690), or [custom agents](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/10724438136858).
This article covers Zendesk acting as an MCP client. In this role, Zendesk connects to external MCP servers, discovers the tools they expose, and uses those tools in action flows, advanced action flows, and AI agents. In this model, Zendesk sends requests to another system to retrieve information or perform actions as part of a workflow. Zendesk can also act as an MCP server in other scenarios. In that role, Zendesk exposes tools or resources that third-party AI agents can use to access Zendesk data or perform actions in Zendesk.

- OAuth is the only supported authentication method for MCP server connections. Only HTTP servers are supported. Stdio transport is not supported.

title: Announcing the general availability of the MCP client
snippet:
Zendesk is excited to announce the general availability of the MCP client, which makes it possible to use the tools on an MCP server in action flows to fetch data and take actions in external systems.

With this release, admins can connect their Zendesk account to MCP (model context protocol) servers. Both public MCP servers from vendors such as Asana, Stripe, or Github, and private MCP servers are supported.
When you connect Zendesk to an MCP server, the MCP client finds all of the tools the MCP server has and lets you choose which ones you want to expose for use in action flows. When used in action flows, the MCP server tools can be used by AI-powered features, such as [auto assist](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/7051314237466), [AI agents](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8966284087066), and [custom agents (EAP)](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/10724438136858), streamlining how you fetch data from and perform actions in external systems and expanding what you can do with Zendesk in your business workflows.

Zendesk understands that there is a lot of setup and maintenance overhead involved in using traditional integrations based on APIs including the need to manage separate connections between each Zendesk feature and the external system and API wrappers for each API endpoint you use.
MCP streamlines this process so you can reuse a single MCP connection across a whole range of features, without needing to create separate API wrappers. It also provides a mechanism for the server to describe all of its tools and make them available for use with a single click.
## What do I need to do?
This feature is available to Zendesk Suite Growth plans and above and Support Team plans and above. To get started, see [Connecting to MCP servers and using MCP tools in action flows](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/10497779528730).
If you participated in the MCP Client EAP, note that MCP connections are now managed on the Connections page in Admin Center. Your MCP connections and any action flows that use them are unaffected, but any browser bookmarks or internal documentation pointing to the previous MCP connections page should be updated.
